source_review.notes: Checked current RFC Editor publications for IPv4 routing, IPv6, Neighbor Discovery, ARP, IPv4 conflict detection, router preferences, address selection and multi-prefix first-hop selection, plus current Linux resilient-next-hop and route-netlink documentation. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; normative protocol rules, Linux interfaces, abstract models, operational guidance and assurance remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked route lookup inputs and typed outputs, neighbor lookup, prefix masks, policy rules, weighted groups, neighbor entries and generation notation.
Reviewed LPM ordering, bounded policy recursion, weighted selection, unresolved queue bounds and multi-generation cache validation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates policy selection, prefix semantics, next-hop choice, neighbor state, resource admission and object lifetime.

evidence: Executed lookup for 10.1.2.33 across default, /8 and /24 routes with different metrics.
Confirmed the /24 wins before metric comparison and stable hash 5 selects 192.0.2.2 from a 2:1 weighted next-hop list.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates one LPM and weighted-selection example only; it implements no policy rules, kernel FIB, resilient ECMP, ARP, ND, device or packet.

evidence: Re-derived canonical prefix matching and maximum matching prefix length before same-prefix tie-breaking.
Checked finite rule evaluation, neighbor object and byte bounds, and conjunction of policy, FIB, next-hop and device generations.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations are subsystem reasoning tools and do not claim a complete formalization of routing, Linux FIBs, ECMP, ARP or IPv6 Neighbor Discovery.

evidence: Reviewed /0 through host routes, noncanonical prefixes, equal metrics, recursive gateways, cycles, negative caches, dead members, extreme weights and adversarial hashes.
Reviewed unsolicited updates, duplicate addresses, unique-neighbor floods, queue pressure, probe exhaustion, timer races, route replacement, interface flap and namespace teardown.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Prefix, policy, recursion, multipath, cache, update, resolution, queue, timer, device and teardown boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced control-state publication, policy lookup, LPM, typed route result, gateway resolution, multipath choice, neighbor lookup, probing, queue drain and link-header construction.
Verified canonical input, deterministic ordering, live generations, scoped keys, validated updates, bounded queues, route revalidation and dependency-ordered teardown.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats policy, prefixes, routes, next-hop groups, devices, neighbors, queues and timers as coupled but independently validated resources.

evidence: Reviewed RIB/FIB separation, policy routing, LPM, typed actions, recursive gateways, ECMP, RCU lookup, ARP, ND, unresolved queues, garbage collection and teardown.
Constructed counterexamples for metric-before-prefix, output-interface-as-route, hash-match-as-live, advertisement-as-reachability and per-neighbor-limit-as-global-bound.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable routing and neighbor obligations, not a formal proof of Linux, a routing protocol, network topology, ARP/ND deployment or security policy.

evidence: Audited uses of installed, published, matched, selected, eligible, resolved, reachable, stale, probed, failed, queued, drained and retired.
Confirmed standards rules, Linux behavior, abstract models, recommendations, tests and assurance claims remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: A route match is not labeled neighbor resolution, a mapping is not labeled reachability, RCU visibility is not labeled escaped-object lifetime and transmit preparation is not labeled delivery.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-075/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, toolchain and environment for the route and next-hop selection model.
Reviewed required namespace, policy, FIB, group, device, neighbor, timer, link, workload, fault and observer evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes one abstract selection only; it provides no evidence for Linux routing, ECMP resilience, ARP/ND correctness, spoof resistance, teardown or performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed forwarding as composition of a typed policy/LPM route result with a separately scoped neighbor-resolution state machine and lifetime proof.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed current route and neighbor mechanisms as implementable concerns, including immutable publication, generations, resilient groups, NUD, hierarchical queue limits, revalidation and teardown. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from RIB/FIB and canonical prefixes through policy, typed routes, next hops, ECMP, caches, ARP/ND, queues, reachability, garbage collection and testing, followed by twelve obligations, sixteen trade-offs, twenty-five misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, IETF, Linux networking, routing-vendor, network-operator, security, performance, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
